transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I just don’t feel like doing anything anymore—not cooking, not music, not even playing dominoes with my friends. It's like all the drive I used to have is just gone.
Can you tell me more about when you first noticed this lack of interest in activities, was it sudden or did it come on gradually?

It came on gradually over several months, rather than all of a sudden. It really started building up after we moved from our old house in Las Piedras to this new apartment about a year and a half ago. I just felt so out of place in the new area, and my interest in everything slowly slipped away.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since you started feeling this way, such as eating more or less than usual, or sleeping more or less than you used to?

During those "high" times when I feel overcharged, I'll sleep only two or three hours a night and still feel completely wired and full of energy. As for my appetite, I haven't noticed a big change in how much I eat, though I've completely lost the drive to cook.
You mentioned feeling 'overcharged' at times, can you describe more about what happens during those periods, such as feeling extremely happy, irritable, or restless?

Yes, during those times I feel like a motor that won't turn off, talking nonstop and joking, but then I can suddenly flip and snap at my family over little things like how they fold the towels. I also get so restless that I can't sit still, cleaning the apartment or rearranging closets at midnight and starting multiple projects that I never finish.
Can you tell me more about how long these 'high' or 'overcharged' periods typically last, and do you experience any periods of feeling extremely low or depressed that last for days or weeks?

Those overcharged spells have kept coming back and lasting quite a long time over this past year, much longer than the quiet stretches. I don't really feel deeply sad or depressed, but during the times I'm not high, I just feel completely flat, tired, and empty of any spark to do anything.
Can you estimate how many days or weeks you typically spend in these 'high' or 'overcharged' states versus the 'flat' states, and do these episodes follow a pattern or cycle?

Ever since we moved here, those high, overcharged spells have kept coming back and lasting for weeks at a time, taking up most of this past year. But there were also a couple of times, lasting at least two or three weeks, where I didn't feel high or low, just completely flat and tired. Even during those flat times, I still heard that man's voice calling my name and felt like the neighbors were watching me.
Can you tell me more about the voice you mentioned, like what it sounds like and what it says when it calls your name?

It is a man's voice that I hear clear as day, especially when I'm alone in my room with the radio off. He calls my name and comments on everything I am doing, sometimes telling me that I am failing my mission. Nobody else can hear him, and it doesn't sound like it is coming from outside the room at all.
Have you ever believed that the voice you hear is real, or have you always known it was just a voice in your head?

To be honest, it feels completely real to me when it happens, like a physical person is right there in the room with me. Even though I know nobody else can hear it, it is so clear as day that I can't help but believe it's real. He is constantly commenting on what I'm doing and telling me I'm failing my mission, and it's very hard to ignore.
Have you ever experienced any periods where you did not hear the voice or have these beliefs about the neighbors watching you, and if so, did those periods coincide with your 'high' or 'flat' states?

Actually, I hear that man's voice and feel watched during both my "high" energy times and my "flat," quiet times. These experiences don't seem to go away based on how I'm feeling; they have been happening pretty consistently regardless of my mood.
Have you ever acted on the instructions or comments made by the voice, or have you felt compelled to respond to it in any way?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, but I don't think I have ever acted on what he tells me to do. Sometimes I do talk back to him when I hear him, though, and my daughter says she catches me arguing or talking to myself in the hallway.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you saw, smelled, tasted, or felt things that weren't there, besides hearing the man's voice?

No, I haven't seen, smelled, tasted, or felt anything else like that. It is really only that man's voice that I hear when I'm alone in my room with the radio turned off. Nothing else like that happens to me.
Have you ever believed that you have special powers, are on a mission, or have a special identity, aside from feeling like you're failing your mission as the voice comments?

Yes, I do sometimes feel that way. I believe God saved me from my fall because I'm meant to be a special messenger for the neighborhood. I've even felt like I could run the entire church better than the priest if they would just listen to my ideas.
Can you describe more about what you mean by being a 'special messenger' and how that relates to the voice you hear and your feelings of being watched?

I believe God kept me alive after my fall because I have a special mission as a messenger for our neighborhood, and I feel I could run the church better than the priest. But that voice constantly calls my name to tell me I am failing this mission, which makes me feel very pressured. I'm convinced the neighbors and churchgoers are watching my every move, using hidden tests in my daily life to see if I am unfit to live on my own.

Can you clarify if the voice you hear and the beliefs about being a special messenger or being watched are present during both your 'high' and 'flat' states, and if they seem to influence your mood or energy levels in any way?

Yes, I experience them in both states. On my high days when I am buzzing around cleaning, the voice still tells me I'm failing my mission and I feel watched by the neighbors. Even during those flat, quiet weeks when I have no energy at all, I still hear him commenting on me and feel convinced I'm being tested, so it doesn't really change with my mood.

Can you describe if there are any distinct boundaries or transitions between your 'high' and 'flat' states, or if they tend to blend together, and how the voice and your beliefs about your mission and being watched relate to these states?

Sometimes I can flip from being wired to feeling flat very quickly, but the voice and the testing never really stop. On my high days when I'm buzzing around cleaning, I still hear him saying I'm failing my mission and feel the neighbors watching me. Even during those quiet weeks when I'm just flat and tired, that voice and the feeling of being tested stay with me the whole time.

Can you tell me if the voice you hear and your beliefs about being a special messenger or being watched seem to be directly related to your 'high' or 'overcharged' states, or if they are separate experiences that coexist with your mood episodes?

They seem like separate things that just happen at the same time, because they don't depend on how much energy I have. On my high days when I'm busy cleaning, the voice still tells me I'm failing and I feel watched, but even during those long, flat weeks when I don't feel high or low at all, I still hear him commenting and feel convinced the neighbors are testing me.

Do you think the voice you hear and your feelings of being watched are more closely related to your own thoughts and feelings, or do they seem to be coming from outside of yourself, and how do you think they relate to your 'high' and 'flat' states?

The voice sounds very clear and real, though I know it doesn't actually come from the outside. It happens during both my high days when I'm buzzing around cleaning, and my flat days when I feel tired and down. It just stays with me regardless of how my mood is.

Can you help me understand if the voice you hear and your beliefs about being watched or having a special mission are more prominent or influential during your 'high' or 'overcharged' states, or if they remain constant regardless of your mood?

On my "high" days when I'm buzzing around and overcharged, that voice is still right there calling my name and telling me I'm failing my mission, and I feel watched by the neighbors. But even during those quieter, flatter stretches this past year when I didn't feel high or low at all, I still heard that man's voice and stayed convinced people were secretly testing me.

Do you think the voice and your beliefs about being watched or having a special mission are directly connected to your mood, or do they seem like separate issues that you're dealing with at the same time?

It feels like both, because they happen during my high-energy times but also completely on their own. When I am buzzing around, I still hear the voice and feel like I am on a mission while being watched. Yet, during those long, flat periods where my mood isn't high or low at all, I still hear that man's voice and feel convinced people are testing me.
Have you ever had a period where the voice stopped or significantly decreased for a while, and if so, did that coincide with any changes in your 'high' or 'flat' states?

No, the voice hasn't really stopped or gone away. It persists across both my "high" days when I am full of energy and buzzing around, and those "flat" stretches when I feel down and tired with no mood extremes. It has just stayed pretty constant this whole past year.

Can you clarify if the voice you hear ever tells you to do things that might harm yourself or others, or if it's primarily focused on commenting on your actions and telling you you're failing your mission?

No, the voice has never told me to hurt myself or anyone else. It is just like I described—it calls my name, comments on what I am doing, and tells me that I am failing my mission. It is very tiring to listen to, but it has never told me to do anything harmful.

Can you tell me if you have ever had a period where you did not experience any psychotic symptoms, such as hearing the voice or feeling watched, for at least two weeks, and if so, did that coincide with any changes in your treatment or circumstances?

No, I haven't really had a period where those things went away. Ever since we moved into this apartment, the voice and the feeling of being watched have been pretty constant. I don't think there has been even a two-week stretch where they stopped.
Have you ever experienced a period where both your mood episodes, such as the 'high' and 'flat' states, and the psychotic symptoms, like hearing the voice, completely stopped for at least two weeks?

No, ever since we moved to this new apartment about a year and a half ago, things have never really gone back to normal. I haven't had any period where both the mood swings and the voices or feelings of being watched completely went away at the same time.
Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is controlling your actions or thoughts, or is it more of a commentary on what you're doing?

No, it doesn't feel like it is taking control of my body or forcing my thoughts, but it acts as a very clear commentary. When I am alone in my room, it just calls my name, talks about what I am doing, and tells me that I am failing my mission.

Can you describe if there was ever a time when you experienced a 'high' or 'overcharged' state without any psychotic symptoms, such as hearing the voice or feeling watched, or if these symptoms always occur together with your mood episodes?

No, they always seem to happen together during those times. Even when I am feeling completely buzzed, energetic, and talking nonstop, I still hear that man's voice calling my name and telling me I'm failing. I also stay convinced that the neighbors are watching my every move.
Can you confirm if you have ever experienced a distinct period of at least two weeks where you did not have any 'high' or 'flat' mood episodes and also did not hear the voice or feel watched?

No, I have never had a period where everything completely stopped like that. Since we moved here a year and a half ago, things have never gone back to normal. Even during those stretches when my mood was neither high nor low, I still heard that man's voice and felt like I was being watched.

Have you ever experienced a period where your mood episodes, such as the 'high' and 'flat' states, occurred without any psychotic symptoms like hearing the voice or feeling watched, or do these symptoms always coincide with your mood swings?

No, I haven't had a time where the mood states happened without those experiences. During my high, energetic days, I still hear the voice and feel watched, and even during the flat, quiet stretches when my mood isn't high or low, those things still persist.
Can you confirm if there was ever a period where you experienced psychotic symptoms, such as hearing the voice or feeling watched, without any 'high' or 'flat' mood episodes?

Yes, there were a couple of long stretches over the past year when I did not feel particularly "high" or "down" in my mood. Yet, during those times, I still clearly heard that man's voice commenting on me and remained convinced that the people in the building were secretly testing me.
Can you tell me if the voice you hear and your feelings of being watched ever completely stop during your 'high' or 'flat' states, or are they always present to some degree?

No, they never completely stop; they are always there to some degree. On my high days when I am buzzing around and cleaning, I still hear that voice and feel watched. Even during those flat stretches when I feel tired and down, those same feelings and the voice persist.

Can you clarify if the voice and your feelings of being watched have ever changed in intensity or frequency in direct relation to the severity of your 'high' or 'flat' states, or if they have remained relatively constant regardless of your mood?

They have stayed pretty constant and don't really change, no matter how my mood shifts. Even during those flat, quiet weeks when I don't feel high or low, I still hear the man's voice and feel like the neighbors are testing me. And on those highly energetic days when I'm buzzing around, those same experiences are still just as strong.
